Abstract
It can be hard to know how kids feel, but if we do, we can develop systems that are emotionally
savvy and can make learning, mental health, and even computer gaming better. Adults can tell
how someone is feeling by looking at their face, but it's usually easier to read kids' emotional
reactions than it is for adults. The research suggests that a hybrid deep learning model that takes
both space and time into consideration can help with this issue. We can use a Convolutional Neural
Network unlawfully to see how expressions change over time in sequences and learn a lot about
the space from facial pictures. The CNN-LSTM combination model is based on a precise set of
children's facial expressions that show six emotions: happy, melancholy (the sense of good or
unpleasant emotions), anger, fear, surprise, and neutrality. Based on the findings of trials, this
technique is better and more reliable than the LSTM model and CNN (clinic model for human
behavior) in a number of samples. There is proof in the real world that the claim is true. The
technique typically works, but it has difficulties with confused faces, lousy lighting, and a lot of
distinct emotional expressions. This plan isn't flawless, though. The model is meant to work
without any extra hardware, though, so it may be utilized in places with minimal resources, like
schools, telemedicine, and mobile apps. The results reveal that there are numerous conceivable
uses for them, such as affect-aware" learning settings, mental health monitoring, smart tools, and
interactive platforms that are safe for kids. This study reveals that automated facial expression
analysis is a quick and uncomplicated way to find out how youngsters see themselves.

Abstract
Modern web applications demand sophisticated performance optimization strategies that adapt
to real-world usage patterns. This research introduces a novel analytical approach that
combines machine learning with web performance metrics to identify and prioritize
optimization opportunities. Unlike conventional methods reliant on static rules, this
methodology dynamically evaluates over 30 technical and user-centric metrics, including Core
Web Vitals, network timing data, and engagement indicators to uncover actionable insights.
The study employs explainable AI techniques to interpret model decisions, enabling developers
to understand which optimizations yield the greatest impact for specific website architectures.
Rigorous validation using real-world datasets confirms the method’s effectiveness in
correlating technical improvements with measurable user experience gains. Key outcomes
include a flexible decision-making framework that helps teams:
• Identify high-priority optimization targets based on empirical evidence
• Allocate resources efficiently by focusing on metrics with proven impact
• Validate improvements through statistically sound testing protocols
This work advances web performance research by demonstrating how data -driven analysis can
replace heuristic-based optimization. The approach requires no architectural overhauls, instead
providing teams with actionable intelligence derived from their existing performance data.

ABSTRACT
Rice is among the world's most important staple crops, particularly in Asia. But its outturn
is heavily impacted by numerous leaf diseases that reduce crop quality and yield. Timely
identification and precise categorization of these sickness can help farmers take timely
actions. In this thesis, we propose a deep learning-based automatic rice leaf disease
identification and categorization system. We used a CNN-based approach with experiments
on models VGG19, and a custom Sequential CNN model. Our dataset used thousands of
labeled images from publicly available rice disease datasets achieved an accuracy of 97%
(Sequential CNN) and an accuracy of 91% (VGG19). The system has promising
performance and can be incorporated into mobile applications to facilitate real-time disease
diagnosis in the field. We employed image preprocessing methods like resizing,
normalization, and augmentation to utilized the model performance. We tested the model's
performance using typical classification metrics and confusion matrices. Based on our
findings, this system can assist in reducing the need for expert consultation and manual
inspection. Overall, the suggested method enhances the expanding field of AI-driven smart
agriculture and offers a scalable solution for rice cultivation disease management.
Keywords: CNN, Deep Learning, Image Processing, Feature Extraction, Rice Disease
Detection, Classification, Real Time Detection, Rice Leaf Analysis, Automated Diagnosis

ABSTRACT
Rice is among the most widely consumed staple foods, especially across Asia. Accurate
classification of rice seed varieties plays a critical role in enhancing crop quality, ensuring seed
purity, and boosting agricultural productivity. In this thesis, we propose a deep learning–based
system for automatic rice seed classification. We employed a CNN-based approach, specifically
utilizing EfficientNetB0 and EfficientNetB3 architectures to distinguish between multiple rice seed
varieties.
Our experiments were conducted on a dataset consisting of thousands of labeled rice seed images.
After applying preprocessing techniques such as resizing, normalization, and data augmentation, the
models were trained and evaluated. The EfficientNetB0 model achieved an accuracy of 53%, while
the EfficientNetB3 model improved the result to 66%, indicating better representation capacity and
feature learning in deeper variants. The model performance was assessed using standard
classification metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrices.
While the overall performance leaves room for optimization, this study demonstrates the feasibility
of using deep learning in the context of rice seed classification. Future work will aim to improve
accuracy by exploring more advanced architectures and increasing dataset diversity. This work
contributes to the development of smart agriculture and offers a foundation for scalable, automated
rice seed quality assessment tools.
Keywords: CNN, Deep Learning, EfficientNetB0, EfficientNetB3, Rice Seed Classification,
Image Processing, Smart Agriculture, Seed Quality Analysis, Feature Extraction

Abstract
Road accidents constitute a serious threat in countries like Bangladesh, often resulting in loss of
life, injuries, and significant economic damage. Although various machine learning models such
as Decision Trees, Random Forest, and Logistic Regression have been used globally for accident
severity prediction, these approaches mainly depend on static datasets and often ignore real-time
conditions and the local context. Furthermore, very few studies attempt to explain the predictions,
making it difficult for traffic authorities to apply them in real situations. This research aims to
address these gaps by proposing a practical framework tailored for Bangladesh. The work reviews
and compares earlier models, identifies their shortcomings, and suggests how AI-based prediction
systems can be enhanced with real-time inputs and explainability tools like SHAP and LIME. By
focusing on accident trends in Bangladesh and showing how data and algorithms can be better
aligned with local needs, this study provides a strong base for future road safety applications.

Abstract
Brain tumor classification is a critical task in medical diagnostics due to its complexity and
life-threatening implications. This study explores the use of deep learning, specifically
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), to classify brain tumors from MRI images. Motivated
by the need for accurate diagnostic tools in rural areas with limited specialist access, we
developed a custom CNN and compared its performance with the pre-trained VGG16 model.
The dataset was augmented and preprocessed to enhance generalization. Results show that the
custom CNN achieved 94% accuracy, significantly outperforming VGG16's 25%. These
findings highlight the potential of tailored CNN models in supporting AI-assisted diagnostics,
especially in underserved healthcare settings.
Keywords:Classification of brain Image, Image recognition, Machine learning, Deep learning

1. Introduction
This section presents the background, problem statement, objectives, and significance of the research.
 Background of the Study:Over the past few decades, machine learning and artificial intelligence (AI) have
opened a new horizon in medical science.And the Deep learning is a part of machine learning which is the main
base of my thesis. In particular, they have emerged as effective technologies for the detection and classification
of brain tumors. Without accurate and timely diagnosis, a patient’s life may be at serious risk. In developing
countries like Bangladesh, it is often difficult to ensure the presence of experienced doctors in all regions,
especially in rural and remote areas. In such situations, a reliable automated system can assist doctors—
especially newly appointed and less experienced physicians—in making more accurate decisions.
 Problem Statement:Due to the shortage of experienced neurospecialists in rural areas, and the delay or
inaccuracy in brain tumor classification, patients often do not receive proper treatment. Although research has
been conducted on this issue in various countries, such automated models are still not widely accessible in the
context of Bangladesh or South Asia.
1.1 Justification of the Study:
At present, Deep learning is widely used for cancer detection around the world. In particular, models such as
CNN, VGG, and ResNet have been effectively applied for tumor identification and classification through MRI
image analysis (Saxena et al., 2021; Pereira et al., 2016). However, in the context of Bangladesh or South Asia,
effective and explainable models using local data are still limited. This research aims to address that gap and has
the potential to contribute significantly to rural healthcare in the future.
1.2 Objectives:
The objectives of this research are as follows:
To develop a custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for multiclass classification of brain tumors using
MRI images.To compare the performance of the custom CNN with the pre-trained VGG16 model.To integrate
Grad-CAM in the future to make the model’s predictions more interpretable.
